minutes.headline: Dangerous dog hearing continued to Aug 11 because the complainant and a witness were absent; board also approved fuel tank license and goals.
minutes.summary: The board approved a diesel tank amendment to a Gulf station flammable storage license, a stop sign change, an interim police lieutenant, committee appointments, and a higher town counsel retainer. A long dangerous dog hearing was continued a week because the complainant did not appear. The town manager reported on state aid, capital projects, a grant award and reopening of town buildings, and the board adopted FY21 goals before going into executive session on collective bargaining.

public_comment.topic: Supported the town manager's succession planning goal and asked that the cemetery and parks commissions' custody of their properties also be considered.
Asked how adding diesel at the Gulf station slipped through the approval process.
Asked that tax lien parcels go to the open space committee, gave an update on the stalled town charter bill, and asked how an at-large Capital Planning seat was filled without advertising.

budget_items.what_was_said: Town counsel proposed a monthly retainer increase to adjust for inflation since 2017; the town manager said the legal expense account has enough funds.
Counsel described effective hourly rates in Lunenburg compared with typical municipal rates.
The coalition cut this year's cost, which returns to the higher level in the next two years.
The town was told the state would fund unrestricted general government aid and Chapter 70 at no less than the FY20 level as a baseline.
The town manager gave status of capital projects, including squad 3 pump repair and portable radios, as part of larger costs.
A state bond bill includes money for fire turnout gear and a primary school fire alarm upgrade, awaiting the governor's signature.
A regional application for microloans and food banks was awarded less than requested; Shirley will administer it.

what_happened.line: The dangerous dog hearing was continued to August 11 by roll call vote, all aye, because the complainant and a witness were absent.
The board raised the FY21 town counsel monthly retainer by roll call vote; counsel cited inflation since 2017 and the town manager said the legal account can cover it.
The board amended a flammable storage license to add a diesel tank at the Gulf station on Mass Ave, and approved a stop sign on Goodridge Street at Reservoir Road.
The board ratified an interim police lieutenant, with one abstention, and appointed members to the personnel and agricultural commissions.
The board adopted its FY21 goals and the town manager's goals, and approved the Central Mass Regional Stormwater Coalition agreement.

why_it_matters: The higher town counsel retainer is a recurring legal cost paid from the town budget, mostly taxes, and the board was told existing funds cover it for FY21.
The diesel tank approval and the dog hearing touch neighborhood safety and licensing, and the dog hearing will be heard again with the complainant's testimony still to come.
State aid held at no less than the FY20 level as a baseline, which bears on how much of FY21 must be raised locally.
watch_next: August 11: the continued dangerous dog hearing, with written or live testimony sought from the complainant and a witness.
August 18: earth removal permit renewals, with board members sending written questions to the building commissioner beforehand.
